subject: Business
title: Bubbles and Manias: From Tulips to Tech
description: A micro-lesson that makes Bubbles and Manias: From Tulips to Tech usable.

hook.text: In 1637, a single tulip bulb in Holland sold for more than a house. Then the market collapsed overnight.

buildup.text: A bubble forms when asset prices soar far beyond intrinsic value, driven by speculation and euphoria.

discovery.text: Every bubble follows five stages: displacement, boom, euphoria, profit-taking, and panic.

twist.text: During euphoria, skeptics are mocked. 'This time is different' is the most dangerous phrase in finance.

climax.text: The dot-com bubble, 2008 housing crash, and crypto boom all followed the exact same pattern.

punchline.text: History doesn't repeat. But bubbles always rhyme.

quiz.question: What phrase is commonly heard during a financial bubble's euphoria phase?

details.summary: Financial bubbles occur when asset prices soar far above intrinsic value driven by speculation, herd behavior, and narrative excitement. From Dutch tulip mania in the 1630s to the dot-com crash and crypto booms, bubble dynamics repeat across centuries and asset classes.
details.whyItMatters: Understanding bubble psychology helps investors and entrepreneurs recognize when markets disconnect from fundamentals. The behavioral patterns of euphoria, denial, and panic are remarkably consistent across every documented bubble.
takeaways: Bubbles follow predictable stages from stealth to awareness to mania to crash
Herd behavior and narrative economics fuel asset price disconnection
Every generation experiences bubbles despite knowledge of historical ones

faq.question: Why do bubbles keep happening if everyone knows about them?
faq.answer: Participants believe each bubble is different due to genuine innovations or new paradigms. Social pressure creates fear of missing out. Rational individuals can profit by riding bubbles early. The collective result is irrational even when individual decisions seem logical.

faq.question: What are the common signs that a bubble is forming?
faq.answer: Rapid price increases disconnected from underlying value, widespread public participation by novice investors, easy credit fueling speculation, media hype about a new era, and dismissal of skeptics as not understanding the new paradigm.
